papers.title: Using observational data for personalized medicine when clinical trial evidence is limited.
papers.one_line: An early clinical exposition pairing target trial emulation with transportability and heterogeneity analysis for infertility questions, which states that generalization beyond a trial population cannot in many practical cases be fully addressed by formal methods.
papers.what_was_done: Two infertility cases frame the argument. Where no trial exists, the recommendation is to specify a target trial protocol with eligibility, treatment strategies, assignment, follow-up, outcomes, causal contrasts and analysis plan, and to emulate it in electronic records or claims; a worked mini-protocol compares fresh versus cryopreserved surgically retrieved sperm for clinical pregnancy after IVF and ICSI, with an intention-to-treat contrast of cumulative incidence differences and ratios. Where a trial exists but its participants differ from the practice population, the recommendation is transportability: outcome models fitted in the trial are applied to the covariates of an observational sample from the target population, or trial participation probabilities are estimated, or both are combined for robustness. The article notes that target trials emulable from routinely collected data are necessarily pragmatic, defining interventions broadly, ascertaining outcomes administratively and foregoing blinding. For heterogeneity it observes that jointly considering 20 binary covariates yields more than a million subgroups, and proposes collapsing covariates into effect scores or baseline risk scores. It reviews benchmarking of observational against randomised estimates and reports that good agreement is achievable but that fairly large disagreements occur. No data are analyzed.

future_research.gap: Scientific generalization across populations, treatments and outcomes cannot be fully formalized, so transport methods address only part of the problem.
future_research.quote: cannot, in many practical cases, be fully addressed using formal methods, despite recent theoretical advances

problems.evidence: Transport is described honestly as principled extrapolation, where the machinery accounts for the statistical uncertainty of extrapolating beyond the trial participants. What it does not account for is the layering: the participation model's assumptions sit on top of whatever confounding assumptions the observational sample carries, and the offered sensitivity analyses examine the underlying causal assumptions without separating the sampling layer from the confounding layer or reporting a combined budget.
problems.quote: All methods can be viewed as strategies for principled extrapolation, in the sense that they properly account for the statistical uncertainty involved in extrapolating inferences beyond the population of trial participants.
problems.locator: Transporting the results of clinical trials to new target populations

problems.evidence: Benchmarking is summarized as showing that agreement is achievable while fairly large disagreements still occur, and the inference drawn is that better data and better methods should improve agreement. That is a hope, not a theory: nothing states which features of a successfully benchmarked comparison would predict success on a new question, and the infertility questions the article then proposes to answer by emulation have no benchmark at all.
problems.quote: good agreement between observational studies and clinical trials is possible, but fairly large disagreements do occur
problems.locator: Using observational data to emulate target trials

problems.evidence: The comparisons underpinning the agreement claim are described as matching already completed studies run in different populations using only what the published literature reported, with no patient-level data, no shared protocols and no harmonized confounding control. Agreement judged on that basis is a label attached to a pair of published numbers, not a calibrated comparison of estimands, and the article says so while still resting the case for emulation on it.
problems.quote: Most comparisons have relied on matching already completed observational and randomized studies conducted independently in different patient populations, using the incomplete information available in the published literature
problems.locator: Using observational data to emulate target trials

problems.evidence: Subgroup estimation is where personalization happens and it is where the data run out: 20 binary covariates already generate more subgroups than any study has participants, and studies are powered for main effects rather than between-subgroup differences. The proposed workaround, collapsing covariates into an effect score or a baseline risk score, moves the problem rather than solving it, since the score is fitted where support is densest and read off where it is thinnest.
problems.quote: Furthermore, one-variable-at-a-time subgroup analyses have low statistical power (because most studies are powered to test main treatment effects, not between-subgroup differences) and, unless proper precautions are taken, produce a large number of false-positive results.

problems.evidence: The protocol is presented as a working document that is revised as the data's practicalities become clear, and this is offered as a virtue that keeps the emulation feasible. The consequence is that the trial finally reported was shaped by the dataset, and the article requires no record of the revisions, so a reader cannot tell whether the specified trial preceded the data or was fitted to them.
problems.quote: The protocol is used to guide the conduct of the observational study in an iterative process
problems.locator: Using observational data to emulate target trials

papers.title: Fuzzy Logic Approaches for Causal Inference in Health Care: Systematic Review.
papers.one_line: Across 37 studies applying fuzzy logic to health care questions with causal intent, only 2 used a formal causal inference framework, none of the 17 prediction-model studies assessed with PROBAST+AI achieved low risk of bias, and target trial emulation is proposed as the missing structure.
papers.what_was_done: A PRISMA 2020 systematic review, registered as PROSPERO CRD420251044493, searched six databases and screened 621 records down to 37 studies published between 2014 and 2025 that applied fuzzy modeling in health care with explicit or implicit causal objectives. Fuzzy inference systems, adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference systems, fuzzy analytic hierarchy process variants and fuzzy cognitive maps predominated, across infectious disease, cancer, cardiovascular disease, mental health, occupational health and preterm birth. Fourteen studies included a comparator model: 5 reported fuzzy superiority, 3 comparable performance and 6 gave insufficient detail to judge. Two studies used a formal causal framework, one fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis and one an interval-valued intuitionistic fuzzy DEMATEL-ANP structure. Six more simulated causal mechanisms through expert-built maps without testing necessity, sufficiency or counterfactual dependence. Sample sizes were 13 studies at 1000 or more, 10 at 100 to 999, 10 under 100 and 4 not applicable. Of 17 studies assessed with PROBAST+AI, 9 were high and 8 moderate risk of bias with none low; of 20 assessed with the JBI checklist, 5 were low and 15 moderate. Most relied on internal validation without external benchmarks.

future_research.gap: Fuzzy models applied to observational health data lack the estimand, temporal ordering and intervention definition that a target trial protocol would supply.
future_research.quote: future research would benefit from explicitly incorporating TTE

problems.evidence: Across 35 of the 37 studies the causal content lives in the model's architecture and in the expert knowledge encoded in its rules, never in a stated identification argument. Flexibility and interpretability are treated as the qualification for causal interpretation, so a system that tolerates imprecision and encodes expert structure is read as having earned a causal reading it never derived. Only two studies stated assumptions and thresholds explicitly.
problems.quote: In most studies, fuzzy logic was applied primarily for predictive or associative purposes, with causal assumptions embedded implicitly within model architecture or domain expertise rather than explicitly articulated or empirically evaluated.

problems.evidence: Six studies built expert mappings or cognitive maps that simulate a causal mechanism while testing none of the conditions that would make the mechanism identifiable, and their causal claims are reported alongside those of the two studies that did state thresholds and validation strategy. Nothing in the reporting distinguishes an assumption that was checked from one that was assumed, which is why the review had to reconstruct the distinction itself.
problems.quote: Six additional investigations relied on expert-based mappings, FCM, or influence structures to simulate causal mechanisms without formally testing necessity, sufficiency, or counterfactual dependence

problems.evidence: Only 14 of 37 studies compared their model against anything, and of those 6 reported too little for the comparison to be assessed, leaving 5 claims of superiority and 3 of parity as the entire evidence base for choosing a fuzzy estimator over a conventional one. Most validation was internal, on small to medium datasets, without external benchmarks, so no default is defensible and no study was required to show that its modeling choice changed nothing.
problems.quote: The remaining 6 studies provided comparative analyses with insufficient methodological or statistical detail to support firm conclusions regarding relative effectiveness

problems.evidence: The gap identified is between a method's theoretical capacity to represent causal structure and what its applications actually establish, and the review attributes that gap to design, validation and reporting rather than to the method. This is the same substitution the catalog tracks under a different name: the class of model is taken as the credential, and the assumption burden of each individual analysis goes unexamined, with the risk-of-bias ratings showing none of 17 prediction studies reaching low risk.
problems.quote: Taken together, these findings reveal a marked disconnect between the theoretical capacity of fuzzy logic to represent causal structure and its prevailing empirical use in health care research.

papers.title: Starting right: aligning eligibility and treatment assignment at time zero when emulating a target trial.
papers.one_line: Methodological guidance that discretizes each person's record into intervals and routes an emulation to a single trial, to sequential trials, or to cloning depending on how many eligible intervals and how many compatible strategies a person has, while stating that this alignment does not protect against unmeasured confounding, measurement error or missing data.
papers.what_was_done: Three target trial protocols for metformin versus never metformin on all cause mortality in newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes are specified and emulated on a hypothetical longitudinal healthcare database. The emulation procedure is: split each person's record into intervals, mark the intervals at which eligibility is met, and at each such interval classify the person into every treatment strategy compatible with data up to that interval. For the worked example person, diagnosed at month 2 with metformin fills at months 4 and 5, target trial 1 yields one time zero at month 2; target trial 2 with a three month eligibility window yields three replicates starting at months 2, 3 and 4; target trial 3 with a three month grace period yields two clones both starting at month 2. Variance after replication or cloning is handled by one sentence naming robust variance estimation or bootstrapping. A decision diagram routes an analysis on three binary questions: eligible at multiple intervals, assignable at multiple intervals, and strategies indistinguishable at an eligible interval. In the head-to-head variant, eligible individuals who never initiate any treatment cannot be assigned and drop out of the comparison, which is presented as a choice between two different target populations. No data are analyzed, no simulation is run, and no quantity is reported for how much any of these routing choices moves an estimate.

future_research.gap: Correct alignment at time zero leaves unmeasured confounding, measurement error and missing data untouched, and no procedure is given for them.
future_research.quote: Although aligning eligibility and treatment assignment at time zero avoids design biases, it does not protect against data inadequacies such as unmeasured confounding, measurement error, and missing data.

problems.evidence: The interval width that defines the whole analysis is set by a judgment call illustrated with two examples, hourly for intensive care and weekly or monthly for a diabetes drug, and no rule states how to check that a chosen width is short enough. The three month grace period in target trial 3 is likewise asserted as part of the protocol rather than derived from anything outcome-blind, even though it is exactly what makes the two strategies indistinguishable and forces cloning.
problems.quote: The interval width needs to be sufficiently short to capture changes in eligibility criteria, treatments, and outcomes.
problems.locator: The target trial: eligibility and assignment to treatment strategies

problems.evidence: Cloning multiplies the example person into two clones and sequential emulation multiplies the same person into three replicates, and the entire treatment of the resulting dependence is a parenthetical naming two options. Nothing states which of robust variance and the bootstrap is correct under cloning plus censoring plus inverse probability weighting, nor what either costs on a database large enough to need monthly intervals over years.
problems.quote: The statistical analysis should then account for the repeated use of the same individual (eg, by using robust variance estimation or bootstrapping)
problems.locator: Target trial 3: Eligibility met once, treatment strategies indistinguishable at eligibility

problems.evidence: Sequential emulation is presented as the statistically efficient option relative to picking one time zero at random, and the only consequence acknowledged is repeated use of the same individual, handled at the variance step. The example person contributes three replicates with three different calendar start dates, yet nothing addresses that the replicates start under different calendar conditions or that the efficiency gain comes from the same person appearing three times.
problems.quote: We can then pool the data from all the sequential trials for a joint analysis with appropriate variance estimation to account for the repeated use of the same individual
problems.locator: Target trial 2: Eligibility met multiple intervals, treatment strategies distinguishable at eligibility

problems.evidence: Under cloning the guidance rules out the effect of assignment and leaves only a per protocol effect, estimated by censoring at deviation plus inverse probability weighting for time fixed and time varying confounders. The estimand is therefore a weighted contrast among the subgroup whose data were compatible with both strategies during the grace period, but no statement fixes the summary measure that this contrast licenses, so nothing in the guidance stands between that estimand and a reported hazard ratio.
problems.quote: In this case, the effect of treatment assignment is not relevant because the groups are identical at time zero, and the effect of interest is typically a per protocol effect.
problems.locator: Causal contrasts in the target trial

problems.evidence: The head-to-head case makes an unobservable protocol component explicit: eligible individuals who never initiate any drug cannot be classified, so the analyzed population is the initiators rather than the eligible. Two remedies are offered, a generalisability analysis back to all eligible individuals, or adding the eligibility criterion that a physician determined treatment should be initiated. The second remedy replaces an unobservable clinical judgment with a filled prescription, which is a proxy, and no diagnostic is offered for how far the initiator population sits from the eligible population.
problems.quote: Furthermore, some eligible individuals may never initiate any treatment and therefore cannot be assigned to any treatment strategy of interest, which results in their exclusion from the head-to-head comparison.
problems.locator: Target trial 2: Eligibility met multiple intervals, treatment strategies distinguishable at eligibility

problems.evidence: The decision diagram routes the design choice but stops at the estimator: inverse probability weighting and the plug-in g-formula are offered as interchangeable routes to the same per protocol effect with no criterion for preferring either and no requirement that a study show the choice did not matter. The only caveat attached is that identifying and measuring the time varying prognostic factors may be difficult, which applies equally to both.
problems.quote: An alternative is estimating the per protocol effect using the plug-in g-formula.
problems.locator: Causal contrasts in the target trial

papers.title: A commentary on "Robotic versus laparoscopic surgery for middle and low rectal cancer: a retrospective cohort study emulating the target trial".
papers.one_line: A letter arguing that a published emulation reporting a 3.4 percentage point gain in 3 year disease-free survival for robotic over laparoscopic rectal surgery (86.7% versus 83.3%, HR 0.800, number needed to treat 29.4) cannot support broad adoption because surgeon and centre effects remain confounded with the platform.
papers.what_was_done: The letter responds to a retrospective emulation of a target trial comparing robotic and laparoscopic surgery for middle and low rectal cancer. The reported results are 3 year disease-free survival of 86.7% versus 83.3%, a hazard ratio of 0.800, a number needed to treat of 29.4 to avert one disease-free survival event, positive circumferential resection margins of 2.2% versus 4.2%, and abdominoperineal resection rates of 7.5% versus 12.4%. Three objections are raised: the REAL randomised trial found nearly 50% higher direct surgical cost for robotics, which the emulation does not weigh; effects observed in high-volume expert centres may not extend to general practice, which propensity score matching does not fix; and guideline recommendations require balancing oncologic, functional and cost outcomes rather than a single endpoint. The structural objection is that two of the participating centres performed only laparoscopic surgery, so centre and platform are partially confounded, and that surgeon proficiency effects of the kind documented in the ROLARR trial persist. The proposed remedy is a decision-analytic model estimating 5 to 10 year overall survival and quality-adjusted life-years against costs of surgery, recurrence management and stoma care.

future_research.gap: The surgical quality indicators that favour the robotic platform have never been translated into survival or quality-adjusted life-years.
future_research.quote: their translation into improved long-term survival or quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) remains unquantified

problems.evidence: The two arms are named by equipment, robotic and laparoscopic, but what a patient receives is a surgeon operating a platform, and proficiency is documented in the ROLARR trial as a persistent confounder of exactly this comparison. A 3.4 percentage point difference in 3 year disease-free survival is being attributed to the platform when the treatment version delivered varies with operator experience and no procedure exists that says which operator-platform combinations count as the same treatment.
problems.quote: Moreover, as evidenced in the ROLARR trial, confounding by surgeon proficiency and center-specific factors persists in platform comparisons

problems.evidence: Two of the participating centres offered only laparoscopic surgery, so those centres contribute exclusively to one arm and centre identity is partly collinear with treatment. The multi-centre estimate then averages over sites that were not emulating the same trial, because a site with no robotic capability could not have randomised anyone to it, and the difference attributed to technology may be a difference in centre expertise.
problems.quote: particularly as two participating centers performed only laparoscopic surgery, potentially clustering outcomes according to unmeasured expertise rather than technology

problems.evidence: The estimate comes from high-volume expert centres and is being read as a recommendation for general practice, which requires a transport assumption on top of the conditional exchangeability assumption the matching was meant to deliver. Propensity score matching balances the compared groups within the sampled centres and says nothing about the centres that were not sampled, and no accounting appears for that second layer.
problems.quote: real-world evidence suggests that the benefits observed in high-volume, expert-center studies may not consistently extend to broader practice settings

problems.evidence: The study carries the target trial emulation label and reports a statistically significant survival difference, and that combination was taken as sufficient for a superiority claim. The objection is that the label certifies the alignment of design, not the exchangeability of surgeons and centres, and the residual assumption burden here is large enough that a number needed to treat of 29.4 cannot be read as a treatment effect of the platform.
problems.quote: The current emulation design cannot fully resolve this

papers.title: Real-world comparative effectiveness of SARS-CoV-2 primary vaccination campaigns against SARS-CoV-2 infections: a federated observational study emulating a target trial in three nations.
papers.one_line: A three nation federated emulation running one common pipeline over a shared data model returned restricted mean survival time gains of 35.9, 59.6 and 1.6 days over 365 days, a spread the report attributes to site-specific confounder availability, testing policy and exclusion failure rather than to differing vaccine effect.
papers.what_was_done: Population registries from Aragon (1,143,805 individuals), Brussels and Wallonia (3,948,815) and Finland (5,308,428) were mapped to a common data model and analyzed by an identical pipeline; daily 1:1 propensity score matching of newly primary vaccinated to un- or partially vaccinated individuals over the enrolment window of January to September 2021 produced 755,055, 2,123,328 and 2,588,318 matched pairs. Follow-up ran to 1 September 2022 with the effect measured as a restricted mean survival time difference at 365 days, since proportional hazards did not hold. Documented infection occurred in 34.4%, 26.6% and 15.8% of matched individuals. Primary vaccination extended infection-free time by 35.9 days (34.9 to 37.0) in Aragon, 59.6 (59.3 to 60.0) in Brussels and Wallonia, and 1.6 (1.1 to 2.0) in Finland. The matching covariate set differed by site because variables with heavy missingness were dropped locally: individual socioeconomic status in Aragon; foreign status and pregnancy in Belgium; institutionalized status, foreign status and pregnancy in Finland. E-values suggested unmeasured confounding was implausible in the first two sites and plausible in Finland at 1.691, and a Belgian sensitivity analysis found a 3.2% change in the estimate from adding individual socioeconomic status. Competing risk of death was not modeled; matched pairs were censored when either member died. Protocol, causal model, common data model, synthetic dataset, pipeline and local outputs were deposited.

future_research.gap: The causal model's assumptions are not expected to hold across the whole period, so a one-off emulation cannot settle effectiveness.
future_research.quote: assumptions on our exposure-outcome relationship as defined in the predefined causal model may not hold over time
future_research.locator: Strengths and limitations of the study

problems.evidence: One pipeline over one common data model still produced three different emulations, because each site dropped a different set of matching covariates for missingness: socioeconomic status in Aragon, foreign status and pregnancy in Belgium, and three variables in Finland. The Belgian and Finnish estimates differ by 58 days of infection-free time, and nothing in the design separates that gap into effect heterogeneity versus adjustment-set divergence. Reporting the sites separately avoids an average that would hide this, but leaves the comparison uninterpretable in the same way.
problems.quote: matching was limited to available confounders, and residual confounding might persist as covariates with high or complete missing were excluded as matching factors in the local analyses
problems.locator: Strengths and limitations of the study

problems.evidence: The outcome variable is structurally identical across sites, a registered positive PCR test, and semantically different: Finland tested only symptomatic individuals while the other sites also tested traced contacts and screened. The near-null 1.6 day estimate in Finland is thus not comparable to the 59.6 day Belgian estimate even though both were produced by the same code from the same field of the same model. Shared structure is exactly what the federated design guarantees and exactly what fails to guarantee shared meaning.
problems.quote: resorting to testing data (i.e. PCR tests) to assess infection may have introduced potential misclassification of the outcome as countries deployed different testing strategies during the different stages of the pandemic

problems.evidence: Prior infection was an exclusion criterion, and it was ascertained only from registered PCR tests, so an individual infected without a recorded test is indistinguishable in the data from an individual never infected. Seroprevalence work in these regions indicates recorded cases were a fraction of true circulation, and the failure is named as a candidate explanation for the almost negligible Finnish effect of 1.6 days, tying an unrecorded eligibility criterion directly to a headline estimate.
problems.quote: excluding individuals with a prior SARS-CoV-2 infection to eliminate the element of natural immunity in our study, solely based on registered PCR tests, might not be sufficient

problems.evidence: The E-value was computed per site and benchmarked against a measured association in the same model, the hazard ratio of 2.89 (2.86 to 2.93) for one age category, which converts an abstract sensitivity number into a comparison against a confounder actually present. It flagged Finland at 1.691 as vulnerable. That is one device: no negative control outcome, no negative control exposure, no proxy for the unmeasured socioeconomic gradient outside Belgium, and no validation sample, and the Belgian percentage-change check is explicitly said not to extrapolate to the other sites.
problems.quote: The estimated E-values suggest that unmeasured confounders are unlikely to challenge causality in Aragon and Brussels and Wallonia, but unmeasured confounding is plausible in Finland
problems.locator: Strengths and limitations of the study

problems.evidence: Death is handled by censoring both members of a matched pair when either dies, and the justification offered is that death rates were similar across countries so the cross-country comparison is unaffected. That is an argument about comparability of a bias, not an identification argument: the restricted mean survival time at 365 days is being computed in a world where death has been removed by censoring rather than treated as a competing event with a stated assumption.
problems.quote: Another limitation of the study is the lack of accounting for competing risks, particularly the risk of death, in the survival analysis
problems.locator: Strengths and limitations of the study

problems.evidence: The deposited objects go well past a methods section: the protocol, the directed acyclic graph, the common data model that carries the phenotype definitions, a synthetic dataset, the executable pipeline and the per-site outputs, with balance diagnostics reported as standardized mean differences in supplementary tables. What is absent is the history: no record of which protocol versions were rejected as the local data proved inadequate, and the site-specific covariate exclusions surface only as prose in the limitations rather than as a versioned decision.
problems.quote: The research objects generated during the current study (i.e. a study protocol, a data management plan, a causal model, a common data model, a synthetic dataset, an interoperable analysis pipeline, and local outputs) are available from Zenodo

papers.title: Beyond Accuracy: Methodological Advances for Assessing the Clinical Impact of Infectious Disease Diagnostics.
papers.one_line: A methods review of infectious disease diagnostics arguing that a test's effect runs entirely through clinician behaviour, that confounding-adjusted estimates are absent from almost all observational rapid-test studies, and citing RCT-DUPLICATE's 75% and 66% agreement rates as the warrant for the target trial framework.
papers.what_was_done: The review surveys design and analysis options for establishing the clinical impact of in vitro diagnostic tests in infectious disease. It notes that unlike drugs, diagnostics are approved and scaled on accuracy alone, and that their effectiveness is determined by where, how and with whom they are used and by what clinicians do with the result. Existing systematic reviews of rapid diagnostic test designs are reported as showing moderate to substantial bias potential and low quality of evidence, with confounding-adjusted estimates missing from almost all such studies. The target trial framework is recommended for observational evaluations, supported by RCT-DUPLICATE, in which emulations of 32 randomised trials reproduced statistical significance in 75% and the effect estimate in 66%. Directed acyclic graphs and clinical judgment are recommended over stepwise selection for choosing adjustment variables, with worked examples of variables that are confounders for antibiotic questions but not for diagnostic questions. Analyses restricted to test-positive patients are criticized as conditioning on future unknowable information and as vulnerable to immortal time. Alternatives discussed include intention-to-diagnose, modified intention-to-treat, desirability of outcome ranking frameworks, benefit-risk frameworks and hybrid effectiveness-implementation designs. Payer evidence needs are framed through the Fryback and Thornbury levels used by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services.

future_research.gap: Both randomised and observational evaluations answer whether a test can work in one centre at one time, not whether it does work as practice, therapies and clinician trust change.
future_research.quote: observational studies are still limited akin to RCTs in answering “can it work” for a setting at a point in time rather than “does it work”

problems.evidence: A diagnostic has no effect except through what a clinician does with the result, so the treatment strategy in any target trial of a test is a composite of assay, reporting pathway and prescriber response, and none of these is specified in the studies reviewed. The assignment unit is equally unresolved: tests are deployed at the level of a laboratory or a shift, illustrated by business-hours-only coverage, while outcomes are measured on patients. Clinician learning over time is named as a further reason the treatment is not stable.
problems.quote: Unlike pharmaceuticals, the effectiveness of IVDs depends on how results are used to inform clinical decisions highlighting the need for diagnostic stewardship and implementation considerations throughout a test's lifecycle.

problems.evidence: The evidence offered that emulation works is two agreement percentages over 32 trials, 75% on statistical significance and 66% on the effect estimate, with no statement of how far the disagreeing emulations were from their trials or on what scale agreement was declared. A binary agree or disagree tally cannot say whether an emulation was calibrated, and it is being carried into a new field, diagnostics, as though it were a transferable performance figure.
problems.quote: this approach has yielded the same statistical significance in 75% of RCTs and the same effect estimate in 66% of studies in the RCT-DUPLICATE Initiative of 32 RCTs

problems.evidence: Payers and health technology assessment bodies agree that accuracy alone cannot establish clinical effectiveness, which is a negative criterion, and no positive one is on offer. Premarket submissions supply technical and diagnostic accuracy at the first two levels of the framework payers use, and what would suffice above that is left to each payer, so a manufacturer has no threshold to design an evaluation against.
problems.quote: A review of Health Technology Assessment (HTA) methodologies demonstrated that while approaches may vary, there is a consensus that accuracy alone cannot establish clinical effectiveness
problems.locator: Evidence generation for coverage and reimbursement

problems.evidence: The framework is introduced as the remedy for a literature judged to have moderate to substantial bias potential, and what it is credited with is the avoidance of common pitfalls with many biases. In the same passage the concrete deficiency is that confounding-adjusted estimates are missing from almost all rapid-test studies, which no design framework fixes. Adopting the label is thereby offered as progress on a problem the label does not address.
problems.quote: the application of the “target trial framework,” or designing an observational study to emulate RCT data measurement and analysis, facilitates the avoidance of common pitfalls with many biases

problems.evidence: A common analysis restricts the study population to patients whose test came back positive, for example influenza-positive patients, which defines eligibility on a variable realized after the intervention. The consequence stated is twofold: the resulting contrast corresponds to no deployable intervention, and the selection can create immortal time, as when patients whose result returned during their emergency department stay are compared against an entire standard-of-care arm.
problems.quote: While these data are informative in elucidating mechanisms of clinical benefit of the test, they are conditioning on future unknowable information

problems.evidence: Adjustment models in this literature are reported as not stating whether they are aiming at description, prediction or causation, and as not following any established development procedure, which means the estimator is chosen without a declared target. The corrective recommended is qualitative, use graphs and clinical judgment rather than stepwise selection, and no requirement is proposed that a study demonstrate its modeling choice did not move the estimate.
problems.quote: adjustment models often neither specify their goal (ie, description, prediction, or causation), nor follow established recommendations for model development

papers.title: Improving reporting of observational studies of interventions: The TARGET guideline.
papers.one_line: A 21-item reporting checklist for target trial emulations, scoped to parallel-group individually randomised target trials with baseline confounder adjustment, introduced against a background in which 70% of a representative sample of 200 observational drug studies from 2022 carried at least one design-related bias.
papers.what_was_done: The TARGET checklist recommends a minimum set of 21 items for reporting an observational study that explicitly emulates a target trial, with a website carrying templates and resources, an explanation and elaboration document in preparation, and non-English translations under way. Its stated scope is a parallel group, individually randomised target trial analyzed with adjustment for baseline confounders. The motivating figures are that 70% of a representative sample of 200 observational studies of drug interventions published in 2022 had at least one design-related bias, and that the protocol and emulation components of published emulations are poorly reported. The framework is described as endorsed by the UK National Institute for Health and Care Excellence and by the European Medicines Agency. Uptake strategies proposed are journal recommendation or mandate of a completed checklist at submission and use by peer reviewers. No evaluation is reported of whether checklist adherence changes reporting completeness or study validity, and known barriers to reporting-guideline uptake are acknowledged as likely to apply.

future_research.gap: Whether the checklist is adopted, and whether adoption improves anything, is unknown and the usual guideline uptake barriers are expected.
future_research.quote: Whilst adherence to TARGET may result in more complete and consistent reporting, there will likely be challenges with its uptake
future_research.locator: The role of the TARGET guideline

problems.evidence: The normal workflow is stated plainly: the target trial is designed iteratively against what the observational data turn out to contain, so the trial being emulated is chosen after the data have been inspected. The checklist then records that trial as though it had been fixed in advance, and no item asks how many iterations occurred or what the data revealed between them. Inference proceeds conditional on a protocol that the data helped select.
problems.quote: The target trial is usually designed iteratively based on the information available in the observational data so that it can be emulated closely, given the data constraints.

problems.evidence: The transparency requirement is aimed at the protocol and at how it was emulated, both of which are end states. Since the protocol is arrived at iteratively against the data, the intermediate protocols that were tried and abandoned are the record that would let a reader judge the selection, and the checklist has no place for them.
problems.quote: For TTEs to inform decision-making in any context, the target trial protocol, and how it was emulated must be transparently reported.

problems.evidence: The scope statement fixes the checklist to a parallel group, individually randomised target trial with baseline confounder adjustment. That excludes the designs where the undiagnosable assumptions concentrate: sequential emulation with repeated participation, cloning under grace periods, censoring for protocol deviation with time-varying weights. A study using any of those reports against a checklist that never asks about them, and a reader gets no instrument that separates the assumptions a diagnostic could test from those it could not.
problems.quote: It provides guidance for reporting observational studies of interventions explicitly emulating a parallel group, individually randomized target trial, with adjustment for baseline confounders.
problems.locator: The role of the TARGET guideline

problems.evidence: Correct application of the framework is credited with eliminating design-related biases and with improving trust in the studies that use it, which moves the label from a statement about one class of bias to a warrant for the study as a whole. The same passage elsewhere concedes that the framework only clears design-related bias and leaves data quality and confounding untouched, so the trust claim rests on a narrower guarantee than it appears to make.
problems.quote: Appropriate application of the target trial framework can eliminate design-related biases and improve trust in the increasing number of published studies investigating the comparative effectiveness of interventions with observational data.

problems.evidence: Two regulators are named as endorsing the framework, and an endorsement of a design framework is not a threshold. Nothing in the checklist or in the endorsements states how much residual confounding is acceptable, what counts as adequate emulation, or how many sensitivity analyses suffice, so the same checklist is satisfied by an emulation whose assumptions are defensible and by one whose assumptions are not.
problems.quote: The target trial framework is endorsed by the UK National Institute of Health and Care Excellence and the European Medicines Agency to maximize the value of observational studies of interventions.

problems.evidence: The premise for a new checklist is that the protocol and its emulation are poorly reported in the current literature, which is a statement about the prose. The remedy is 21 reporting items rather than a requirement to deposit the analysis code, the phenotype definitions that map data to eligibility and treatment, or the weight and balance diagnostics, so the artifacts that would let a reader reproduce the emulation remain outside the standard.
problems.quote: In practice, however, these critical components are poorly reported

papers.title: Moving beyond the prevalent exposure design for causal inference in dementia research.
papers.one_line: A systematic search found 84 of 116 (72%) recent observational cohort studies of dementia-prevention factors used a prevalent exposure design, including 62 of 62 physical activity studies, and a worked target trial protocol is offered as the replacement.
papers.what_was_done: A systematic search covered observational cohort studies of five factors hypothesised to reduce dementia risk: hearing aids, physical activity, antihypertensives, antidiabetics and antidepressants. Of 116 eligible studies, 84 (72%) used a prevalent exposure design; by factor, the proportion using any prevalent exposure design was 62 of 62 for physical activity, 12 of 18 for antihypertensives, 7 of 22 for antidiabetics, 6 of 10 for antidepressants and 5 of 6 for hearing aids, 90 of 116 overall. Three failure modes are worked through on a published leisure-time physical activity case study: interventions that are ill-defined because exposure began at an unspecified time and with an unspecified regimen; survivor bias from depletion of susceptibles, which is argued to bias physical activity effects toward the null and to underlie apparently protective effects of smoking and obesity in this literature; and confounder timing, where time-zero body mass index and comorbidity may be mediators of pre-baseline activity. The proposed alternative specifies eligibility as age 65 and over with dementia, mild cognitive impairment and activity-precluding conditions excluded; a strategy of 100 to 200 minutes per week of vigorous aerobic activity with excusal on contraindication; a no-intervention comparator rather than a sedentary comparator; 10 year follow-up; and a per protocol effect via the parametric g-formula. Time zero is set at the second or a later wave of data collection so that a prior activity measurement exists, with the questionnaire assumed to represent average activity over the preceding 1.5 years.

future_research.gap: Outcome misclassification and confounding by latent preclinical disease are named as the dominant remaining biases in this field and are left unaddressed.
future_research.quote: In dementia research, outcome misclassification and unmeasured confounding by latent preclinical disease, for example, are especially important sources of bias
future_research.locator: Challenges for observational analyses in dementia research

future_research.gap: The proposed design needs longitudinal data on exposure type, duration and intensity that most datasets, particularly administrative ones, do not carry.
future_research.quote: A particular challenge for observational research on dementia, especially concerning time-varying exposures such as physical activity, is the need for rich and high-quality longitudinal data.
future_research.locator: Challenges for observational analyses in dementia research

problems.evidence: The proposal replaces data-driven activity tertiles with a numerical target of 100 to 200 minutes per week of vigorous aerobic activity, which fixes the dose but not the version: walking, jogging and weightlifting are named as regimens that could give different dementia outcomes, and only aerobic activity is specified. No procedure decides which regimens belong in the same class, so the estimand still ranges over an unenumerated version set even after the protocol is written down.
problems.quote: An ill-defined intervention is an intervention which, because it is characterised vaguely in important respects, has many possible versions, at least some of which could result in different outcomes.
problems.locator: Potential issues with prevalent exposure designs: Ill-defined interventions

problems.evidence: A concrete and outcome-blind rule is given: set time zero at the second or a later data collection wave so a prior exposure measurement exists to adjust for past activity and reduce depletion-of-susceptibles bias. That is more than most of the 84 prevalent exposure studies do. It does not choose among the later waves, the grid is fixed at whatever the cohort's 1.5 year cycle happens to be rather than at a clinically motivated interval, and the strategy carries no grace period, so the question of how long an initiation window may be is not reached.
problems.quote: we can overcome this challenge by exploiting the longitudinal design and defining time zero as the time of the second (or later) wave of data collection

problems.evidence: Positivity is handled at the design step by excluding people who could not receive the intervention, listing cardiovascular disease, functional impairment and frailty as exclusions, so the unsupported histories are removed before estimation rather than reweighted. What is missing is any diagnostic: nothing in the proposal reports which remaining covariate histories have little or no support for the 100 to 200 minute strategy, and the per protocol effect is estimated by the g-formula, which will extrapolate silently where support is thin.
problems.quote: Such selective inclusion helps to prevent bias in the observational analysis due to violations of the positivity assumption

problems.evidence: The emulation requires the same eligibility criteria as the target trial, which include absence of mild cognitive impairment and of conditions precluding vigorous activity, and the acknowledgment is that a dataset may simply lack the variables to apply them. In that situation an unrecorded frailty or neurological diagnosis is scored identically to a recorded absence, and the remedy offered is to describe the discrepancy alongside the protocol rather than to measure or bound it.
problems.quote: such an approach could reveal that the observational dataset does not have the data required to emulate the eligibility criteria of the target trial
problems.locator: Challenges for observational analyses in dementia research

problems.evidence: The recommended treatment of the gap between the intended trial and the executed analysis is a side-by-side description highlighting what could not be emulated, which is exactly the narrative state of the art. In the worked protocol the compromises are of different kinds: the outcome is diagnosed by panel review in both columns, the strategy is measured by a questionnaire assumed to represent 1.5 years, and only the per protocol contrast is estimated. Nothing separates the resulting error into scientific-target mismatch, protocol compromise, mapping loss and estimation error.
problems.quote: Describing the key features of the observational analysis alongside the target trial highlights the aspects of the target trial that the observational analysis is not able to emulate.
problems.locator: Challenges for observational analyses in dementia research

problems.evidence: The framework is explicitly denied the status of a guarantee: adopting it fixes design-induced bias in the 72% of studies using prevalent exposure designs while leaving outcome misclassification and confounding by preclinical disease exactly where they were. The distinction being drawn is between what the label certifies and what it does not, and the reason to draw it is that readers otherwise treat the label as the certificate.
problems.quote: The target trial framework is not an automatic solution to all issues in observational analyses.
problems.locator: Challenges for observational analyses in dementia research

papers.title: Methods and reporting of studies assessing the impact of adherence to clinical practice guidelines: a scoping review.
papers.one_line: Of 7952 records screened, only 16 studies have ever assessed the clinical impact of adhering to diabetes, hypertension or spondyloarthritis guidelines, none emulated a target trial, and 13 carried serious or critical risk of bias in how participants entered the study.
papers.what_was_done: A scoping review searched PubMed on 3 March 2023 for studies published since 2013 assessing the impact of adherence to clinical practice guidelines for the pharmacologic management of rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, axial spondyloarthritis, psoriatic arthritis, diabetes and hypertension. Sixteen of 7952 records qualified: diabetes 8, hypertension 6, axial spondyloarthritis 2, and none in the other musculoskeletal conditions, against more than 500 recommendations issued for these conditions over the same decade. Median participants analyzed was 511 (IQR 350 to 10,536) and median follow-up 9 months (IQR 4 to 18). All were cohort studies and none emulated a target trial. Only three clearly reported which recommendations were evaluated while 12 assessed adherence to an entire guideline. Fifteen defined adherence but only nine in enough detail to replicate; the comparator was explicitly defined in five, of which two were not mutually exclusive with the adherence definition. Only three defined a primary outcome and eight evaluated surrogate outcomes only. Thirteen accounted for confounding, most often by regression (11), and six reported a missing data method. Under ROBINS-I, 10 studies selected participants on characteristics observed after the intervention started, nine had start of follow-up not coinciding with start of intervention, and none reported any adjustment for the resulting selection bias, giving critical risk in seven, serious in six and low in three.

future_research.gap: Adherence has no standard definition or measurement, which blocks comparison and synthesis across studies.
future_research.quote: Additionally, future research should aim to standardize how adherence is defined and measured.

future_research.gap: Whether target trial emulation can be applied to guideline adherence questions has not been worked out.
future_research.quote: future research should explore the implementation of the target trial emulation framework and its applicability in the context of assessing the impact of CPGs

problems.evidence: Across 16 studies the same nominal treatment, adherence to a guideline, is operationalized in ways that range from implicit to precise but idiosyncratic, and only nine give enough detail to be reproduced. The comparator fares worse: five define non-adherence explicitly and two of those five overlap with their own adherence definition, so the two arms are not disjoint. Nothing in the field says which operationalizations describe the same treatment, which is precisely a missing equivalence class over versions.
problems.quote: The definitions of adherence and non-adherence varied across studies, ranging from vague or implicit definitions to precise but non-standardized definitions.

problems.evidence: Twelve of 16 studies take the intervention to be adherence to an entire guideline, a bundle of dozens of recommendations that no one can be assigned to as a unit, and only one of those twelve says which recommendation it actually looked at. The assignment unit is also undeclared: adherence is a clinician or practice behaviour scored on patients, so it is unstated whether the trial randomises patients, prescribers or sites.
problems.quote: only three studies clearly reported the recommendations of the CPG that were evaluated and 12 stated that they assessed the impact of adherence to the entire CPG with only one indicating which recommendation was considered

problems.evidence: Ten of 16 studies decided who entered the cohort using characteristics recorded after treatment had started, characteristics judged likely to be influenced by both intervention and outcome, which is selection on a collider. Nine had follow-up starting later than the intervention, admitting prevalent users. No study reported any technique to correct for the resulting selection bias, so the collider structure enters the estimate untouched.
problems.quote: we identified a total of 10 studies that selected participants into the study based on participant characteristics observed after the start of intervention
problems.locator: Results: Confounding factors, statistical considerations, and risk of bias in selection of participants into the study

problems.evidence: Thirteen of 16 studies were rated serious or critical for selection of participants and all 16 were published and are now part of the evidence on whether following guidelines helps patients. Nothing in the design or review process functioned as a stopping rule: a critical rating on the one bias domain that was assessed did not prevent the study from being conducted or reported, and 8 of 16 rested on surrogate outcomes only.
problems.quote: there was critical risk of bias in selection of participants into the study in seven studies, serious risk in six studies, and low risk in three studies
problems.locator: Results: Confounding factors, statistical considerations, and risk of bias in selection of participants into the study

problems.evidence: Guideline developers are expected under the GIN-McMaster checklist to plan evaluation of their guidelines, and only 25% of the recommendations in these conditions rest on high level evidence, yet no body has specified how such an evaluation should be done. The result is 16 studies in a decade with no methodological floor: no required design, no confounding standard, no outcome requirement, and no threshold that would mark an evaluation as inadequate.
problems.quote: However, there are currently no recommendations on the methods to conduct such assessments.

papers.title: Adjacent spillover efficacy of Wolbachia for control of dengue: emulation of a cluster randomised target trial.
papers.one_line: An emulated cluster randomised test-negative trial in Singapore estimated 45% protective efficacy (OR 0.55, 95% CI 0.42 to 0.74) against dengue for residents of sectors merely adjacent to Wolbachia release sites, against up to 77% inside release sites, from a matched cohort of 2,354 pairs drawn from 137,806 tested individuals.
papers.what_was_done: A two-arm cluster-randomised test-negative controlled target trial was specified for Singapore from epidemiological week 1 of 2019 to week 26 of 2022 and emulated on the national dengue test database. Intervention sectors were those sharing a geographic border with actual release sites in four towns covering 607,872 residents; 26 never-treated towns were candidate controls, and constrained randomisation was emulated by drawing 1000 random combinations of 12 townships and keeping those whose pre-intervention dengue incidence matched the intervention towns. Of 137,806 individuals who reported with febrile illness, 58,640 (42.55%) entered matching, and the analytic cohort was 2,354 matched pairs after requiring at least three months of spillover exposure. Test positivity was 12.79% (301 of 2,354) in the spillover arm and 21.07% (496 of 2,354) in controls. G-computation on a matched logistic model gave odds ratios of 0.55 (0.42 to 0.74), 0.54 (0.42 to 0.80) and 0.53 (0.42 to 0.81) at three, six and twelve months of exposure, with no increasing trend across durations. Inference used a cluster bootstrap over towns with 1000 resamples. Six robustness checks were run, including 1000 re-randomisations of the control arm (mean OR 0.56, range 0.46 to 0.69), 100 in-space placebo assignments (mean OR 0.99, range 0.74 to 1.35) and an in-time placebo check (OR 0.93, 0.43 to 1.24). Vector suppression in spillover sectors was tracked by a gravitrap index. Code is available only on request and the underlying data cannot be shared.

future_research.gap: Whether the spillover effect extends to other Aedes-borne diseases cannot be tested in this setting because those diseases are too rare there.
future_research.quote: evaluation of spillover protective efficacies cannot be conducted for other Aedes -borne diseases as those diseases are sporadic in the study setting

future_research.gap: Whether spillover efficacy converges to direct efficacy under sustained exposure is unresolved.
future_research.quote: which can possibly converge in protective efficacy to directly treated sites, if spillover exposure was sustained over time

problems.evidence: Interference is not assumed away here, it is the estimand: the contrast is between residents of untreated sectors adjacent to release sites and residents of untreated towns, giving 45% protective efficacy against up to 77% measured inside release sites in prior work on the same design. That converts a no-interference assumption into a measured quantity for one adjacency ring. What it does not close is the rest of the interference structure: adjacency is binary and geographic, control towns are assumed wholly unexposed with no distance-graded estimate, and the individual-level joint strategy question does not arise because the assignment unit is a sector.
problems.quote: The estimated spillover protective efficacies were also more modest compared to the direct protective efficacies

problems.evidence: A nationally complete testing database shrinks by two orders of magnitude before the estimate is formed: 137,806 tested individuals, 58,640 entering matching, and 2,354 matched pairs surviving the residency and three-month exposure requirements. The entire inference rests on 301 and 496 test-positive individuals, and the confidence interval width across exposure durations, 0.42 to 0.81 at twelve months, reflects that effective sample rather than the size of the source database.
problems.quote: Among 137,806 individuals who reported for febrile illness from EW1 2019 to EW26 2022, in the intervention and control arms, 58,640 (42.55%) were included for matching in the study.

problems.evidence: The intervention has no fixed version: two towns used a phased approach in which release sites grew into adjacent neighbourhoods over three years while two others targeted high-abundance areas, and one town changed sex-sorting methodology and added irradiation partway through. A sector's spillover status therefore depends on when the boundary moved, and the assignment unit is an administrative sector of roughly 0.088 square kilometres defined for surveillance planning. Exposure is then recoded as duration of adjacency, and efficacy does not increase across three, six and twelve months, which is hard to read under any single definition of the treatment.
problems.quote: an expanding release approach was adopted in two large towns (Yishun, Tampines), where release sites were gradually expanded to adjacent neighbourhoods

problems.evidence: The analysis chains constrained-randomisation emulation, high-dimensional matching, g-computation and a town-level cluster bootstrap, and none of it is published: the code statement is an offer to share on request and the test-negative data are contractually unshareable. The 1000 re-randomisations and 100 placebo assignments that carry most of the credibility cannot be checked by anyone outside the group.
problems.quote: All analyses were conducted in R version 4.2.3 and can be shared upon request.

problems.evidence: The three-month threshold does double duty as an exposure definition and an exclusion criterion, and it is set from entomological evidence about suppression lag rather than by any outcome-blind selection rule. Individuals near intervention sites with less than three months of spillover exposure are removed from the cohort by that same constant, so the threshold determines who is analyzed as well as what exposure means, and the three durations reported (three, six, twelve months) are a grid chosen by the investigators.
problems.quote: The 3 or more months exclusion criteria was based on the time taken for Wolbachia interventions to induce suppression of wild-type mosquitoes in areas which have been spillover exposed to the intervention

problems.evidence: Negative controls are built into the workflow rather than appended: 100 in-space placebo assignments treating each control site as if intervened returned a mean odds ratio of 0.99 with 12 positive and 18 negative significant results, and an in-time placebo period before releases began returned 0.93 (0.43 to 1.24). These bound the control-selection and pre-trend threats. They do not touch the threat the design actually carries, differential test-seeking behaviour and outcome ascertainment, for which no proxy, validation subsample or negative control outcome is used.
problems.quote: There were only 12 positive and 18 negative statistically significant spillover intervention efficacies demonstrated in the placebo-control sites out of 100

papers.title: Causal inference in multi-cohort studies using the target trial framework to identify and minimize sources of bias.
papers.one_line: An extension of the target trial framework to pooled multi-cohort analysis that separates within-cohort from across-cohort selection, confounding and measurement bias, and concedes that when cohort-specific estimates disagree the source of the disagreement usually cannot be identified.
papers.what_was_done: The framework is developed for a binary or categorical point exposure and a point outcome, explicitly setting aside sustained strategies, time-to-event outcomes and immortal time. Six directed acyclic graphs pair a within-cohort version with an across-cohort version for each of selection, confounding and measurement bias, with a cohort indicator node standing in for every design feature that is fixed within a cohort and varies across cohorts. The case study re-reads a published pooled analysis of two Australian intergenerational cohorts, the Victorian Intergenerational Health Cohort Study recruited 2006 to 2013 and the Australian Temperament Project Generation 3 recruited 2012 to 2018, estimating the effect of preconception maternal mental health problems in adolescence (13 to 18 years) and young adulthood (19 to 29) on infant emotional reactivity at 1 year postpartum, measured by the Short Temperament Scale for Toddlers with a mean score of at least 4. No new analysis is run and no effect estimates are reported in the text. The recommendations are to include the cohort indicator as a confounder and as an imputation covariate in pooled analysis, to impute separately per cohort when replicating, to repeat analyses under alternative harmonization decisions, and to apply quantitative bias analysis guided by the cohort-expanded graphs. Recruitment for the two original cohorts used different channels, secondary schools versus maternal-child health services, and eligibility for the intergenerational studies required a live birth in the screening window.

future_research.gap: Missingness directed acyclic graphs have been developed only for the single-cohort setting and their identifiability results do not yet cover pooled data.
future_research.quote: Extensions to the multi-cohort setting would be valuable.

future_research.gap: Existing methods for transporting inferences across populations cannot handle confounding and measurement bias at the same time.
future_research.quote: However, extensions are needed to allow simultaneous adjustment for confounding and measurement bias

problems.evidence: Pooling two cohorts is the same operation as pooling two sites, and the concession is unambiguous: a difference between cohort-specific estimates can be real heterogeneity, differential within-cohort emulation failure, or noise, and separating them is usually not possible. In the case study the two cohorts recruited through different channels and in different calendar windows, so the emulations differ in exactly the ways that would produce a spurious difference, and the remedy offered is to include a cohort indicator, which closes a path without measuring the divergence.
problems.quote: An estimated difference in the causal effects across cohorts may thus arise due to effect heterogeneity (an actual difference in the true causal effects), different within-cohort biases in each target trial emulation, or random variability.
problems.locator: Applying the target trial framework in multi-cohort studies

problems.evidence: Harmonization is described as finding a minimum common ground, and the concrete instance is a confounder collapsed to never versus ever completed high school because the two cohorts did not measure maternal education the same way. The pooled variable has the same name and type in both cohorts and a coarser meaning than either source, and the residual confounding this introduces is acknowledged with no method for bounding it. Some confounders existed in only one cohort and were therefore left out of the adjustment set entirely.
problems.quote: measurement of maternal education was not aligned between the VIHCS and ATPG3; hence, there was some loss of information in the blunt harmonized measure of “never completed” vs “ever completed” high school
problems.locator: Application of the target trial framework to the case study: Confounding bias

problems.evidence: The exposure being emulated is maternal mental health problems, and the target trial protocol cannot say what would be assigned: medication, individual therapy or a population-level program are all listed as candidates with no basis for choosing. The framework is applied anyway, on the argument that clear causal thinking is still worthwhile, which leaves a specified target trial whose treatment strategies name a state rather than an intervention and whose confounder selection therefore has no anchor.
problems.quote: While an important intervention target, it is not clear how mental health problems might be changed or treated.
problems.locator: Application of the target trial framework to the case study: Treatment strategies

problems.evidence: The outcome enters the analysis as a binary variable, a maternal-report scale dichotomized at a mean score of at least 4, standing in for what the target trial would obtain by triangulating parent report, clinician assessment and direct observation. Worse, the measurement error is differential by exposure, since mothers with depression may perceive their infants as more reactive, which is drawn as a biasing path in the graph. Regression calibration is named as the correction and is said to need strong assumptions and validation samples, neither of which the cohorts supply.
problems.quote: there is potential for measurement error and thus bias in the use of the STST as a proxy for a more comprehensive assessment of infant emotional reactivity
problems.locator: Application of the target trial framework to the case study: Outcome

problems.evidence: Eligibility for the emulated trial required having become pregnant and delivered a live birth in the screening window, an event ascertained through the health system and occurring after the exposure period of adolescence and young adulthood. Conditioning on it opens a path if pregnancy is a common effect of maternal mental health and of unmeasured causes of infant outcome, which is the stated concern, and the framework offers no resolution beyond noting that the choice of estimand in this setting is unsettled.
problems.quote: where the outcome is defined after a post-treatment index event (here, live birth), the choice of estimand is a complex problem often without a completely satisfactory solution
problems.locator: Application of the target trial framework to the case study: Eligibility criteria

problems.evidence: Each cohort sample is described as imperfectly representing the target population by a different amount, which is the sampling assumption stacked on top of the confounding assumption, and the methods that would formalize the transport step are borrowed from meta-analysis of randomized trials. Those methods assume randomization within trials, so they carry no machinery for the confounding and measurement error that the same section documents in these cohorts, and no accounting exists that keeps the two assumption layers apart.
problems.quote: However, extensions are needed to allow simultaneous adjustment for confounding and measurement bias

papers.title: Estimating the Effects of Lifestyle Interventions on Mortality Among Cancer Survivors: A Methodologic Framework.
papers.one_line: A three step procedure of specification, emulation and deliberate protocol modification applied to 9,107 cancer survivors, in which the estimated 20 year mortality risk difference for a joint physical activity and dietary strategy moves from -4.8 to -13.0 percentage points depending on which modified target trial is emulated, and no individual in the data followed the strategy being estimated.
papers.what_was_done: Two target trials were specified and emulated in the Nurses' Health Study, Nurses' Health Study II and Health Professionals Follow-up Study: sustained adherence to seven physical activity and dietary recommendations, and abstention from alcohol, each versus no intervention, over 20 years after a breast or prostate cancer diagnosis. The analytic sample was 9,107 adults, 5,840 women with breast cancer and 3,267 men with prostate cancer, with 990 deaths in women and 801 in men. Estimation used the parametric g-formula with the GFORMULA macro, and only the per protocol analogue was estimated because an intention-to-treat analogue would track the level of nonadherence. In the main analysis the all-cause mortality risk difference for physical activity and diet was -9.5 percentage points (-11.7, -7.2) in women and -9.2 (-12.5, -5.4) in men against 20 year risks under no intervention of 31.1% and 48.4%. The third step emulated five families of modified target trials that vary eligibility, strategy duration, excusal rules, the outcome and the adjustment set; across these the risk difference spanned -4.8 (-7.5, -2.3) to -13.0 (-15.8, -9.8) in women and -3.0 (-7.4, 0.9) to -12.8 (-17.6, -7.5) in men. Requiring no alcohol produced positive risk differences of 3.3 (2.2, 4.4) in women and 4.8 (1.7, 7.4) in men, and alcohol cessation versus continuation among drinkers produced 4.8 (3.0, 6.6) and 7.4 (3.7, 10.0), a magnitude the report judges implausible on external grounds. Not measured: continuous behavior, detailed time varying cancer treatment, and any observed instance of full adherence to the seven component strategy.

future_research.gap: For alcohol, and possibly other lifestyle strategies, valid estimation from observational data may not be achievable at all because the individuals driving the confounding cannot be identified.
future_research.quote: valid estimation of the effects of alcohol (and potentially other lifestyle strategies) on mortality among cancer survivors may be impossible due to intractable confounding or lack of positivity

future_research.gap: Interval questionnaire measurement leaves behavior and confounders between waves unobserved; continuous ascertainment is named as the remedy and was not available.
future_research.quote: Continuous ascertainment of lifestyle behaviors (e.g., via wearable devices to ascertain physical activity) would further ameliorate these problems.

problems.evidence: The joint strategy requires simultaneous adherence to seven physical activity and dietary components sustained over 20 years, and the data contain not one person who did so; the reported 20 year risk difference of -9.5 percentage points in women is therefore entirely a model extrapolation to histories with no empirical support. What is reported is an adherence count in a supplementary table, not a statement of which covariate histories the g-formula had to invent, and the analysis proceeds unchanged.
problems.quote: No individual adhered to all seven components of the intervention continuously throughout the follow-up
problems.locator: Results: Target trial 1: Physical activity and diet

problems.evidence: The modification that moves the estimate closest to the null excuses individuals from the intervention two or four years before a serious condition is diagnosed, which requires knowing the future. The quantity estimated is therefore not a noisy version of the intended strategy but a different, data-defined strategy whose value depends on three stated assumptions about preclinical disease duration. The estimate under this protocol, -4.8 percentage points in women, sits alongside -13.0 under the protocol closest to prior practice, with no rule for which is the intended target.
problems.quote: This modified protocol cannot be implemented in the real world because it is generally unknown who will develop a serious condition in 2 years.
problems.locator: Step 3: Target trial modifications to investigate lack of comparability

problems.evidence: The spread across modified protocols, -4.8 to -13.0 percentage points in women, mixes at least three distinct things: a change in the scientific target, a compromise forced by unmeasured subclinical disease, and estimation under a stronger comparability assumption. The report attributes the spread narratively to unmeasured confounding and positivity violations but supplies no decomposition that would say how many of those 8.2 percentage points belong to each source.
problems.quote: Estimates were furthest from the null when, as in many prior observational studies, we included people who were unlikely to follow the interventions

problems.evidence: One family of modifications changes eligibility criteria and treatment strategies together rather than one at a time, so two violated conditions are relaxed jointly, and the whole family of estimates is reported as a range rather than a single sensitivity number. What it does not close is the separation of assumption relaxation from estimand change: four of the five modification families alter the causal estimand while only the covariate expansion leaves it fixed, so the reported spread cannot be read as a bias bound.
problems.quote: Modifications I–IV (modifications to eligibility criteria, strategies, and/or outcomes) change the causal estimand, while Modification V (modifications to adjustment covariates) does not.
problems.locator: Step 3: Target trial modifications to investigate lack of comparability

problems.evidence: A negative control outcome, questionnaire non-response, was carried through the same g-formula pipeline as the mortality outcome and returned risk differences close to null, which is a negative control integrated into the emulation rather than bolted on. It is one device on one arm of the problem: no negative control exposure, no proxy variables for the suspected subclinical disease, and no validation subsample, and the null negative control coexists with an alcohol cessation estimate of 4.8 to 7.4 percentage points that is judged implausible.
problems.quote: which we did not expect to be affected by the lifestyle interventions but which could be similarly confounded due to disease severity or health-seeking behavior
problems.locator: Step 3: Target trial modifications, Modifications to outcome

problems.evidence: A dietary target such as under one serving of processed meat per week can be met by many substitutions, and the analysis does not choose among them; the estimand ends up defined by whichever substitutions the three cohorts happened to contain. No procedure declares which substitution patterns count as the same treatment, so the seven component strategy is a label over an unbounded and unenumerated set of versions.
problems.quote: Our estimates should therefore be interpreted as the effects of interventions resulting from a combination of different food substitutions actually observed in the 3 cohorts.
